summary: Thunderbolt dock firmware update resets Ethernet MAC causing SSO certificate bind failure and provisioning loop
environment: prod - docked workstations in NYC site (us-east)
description:
Issue summary:
When devices are re-docked after depot repair (battery replacement + firmware refresh on Thunderbolt dock), the dock-assigned Ethernet MAC changes to a locally administered OUI. The new MAC breaks certificate-based SSO binding (device certificate is bound to inventory MAC), which causes the device to fail the final stages of provisioning and land in a provisioning loop (Intune/SSO handshake fails, device marked non-compliant).

Impact:
- ~18 devices processed through depot in the last 48 hours are failing post-repair provisioning at the corporate NYC docking stations.
- Affected users cannot complete SSO login or access corporate resources until reprovisioning or manual MAC override.
- Potential audit/compliance risk if devices are marked non-compliant.

Environment:
- Prod docking racks at NYC office (us-east).
- Dock model: Dell TB18D with firmware v1.04 applied by depot technician.
- Host models: Dell Latitude 7430 (Windows 11 22H2 with corporate image).
- Provisioning flow: SCCM -> Intune autopilot staged -> cert enrollment via SCEP -> SSO cert binding to MAC in asset inventory.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Depot performs battery replacement + applies latest dock firmware from vendor package (v1.04).
2) Device returned, user docks at corporate station and boots.
3) Device starts provisioning; Intune enrollment initiated.
4) Certificate enrollment fails with mismatch; backend compares MAC in asset inventory vs MAC presented by NIC.
5) Device fails SSO binding and retries provisioning, eventually flagged non-compliant.

Observed logs & evidence:
- Intune enrollment logs: "CertificateBindingError: MAC_Mismatch" (correlation id: 0a3b-7c9f).
- Asset DB entry (pre-repair): mac=00:1A:4B:12:34:56, post-dock log on host: mac=02:5E:AC:77:11:22 (locally administered bit set).
- Windows event viewer: AAD SCEP enrollment error 0x80070005 at 10:12:23.
- USB/Thunderbolt vendor diag from depot: dock firmware v1.04 applied successfully; no errors in vendor tool.
- Packet capture from docking switch shows link up with new MAC; switch port learned 02:5E:AC:77:11:22.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: dock firmware change is enabling MAC randomization or overriding host NIC MAC with a locally administered address.
- Confirmed via walk-up test: re-dock a known device with previous MAC bound certificate; observed MAC flip once dock firmware is applied.
- Verified asset inventory still records host NIC MAC (pre-repair) which no longer matches observed MAC when dock is connected.
- Checked vendor release notes for TB18D v1.04: mentions 'improved NIC failover' but no explicit MAC randomization note.
- Tested with another dock (v1.02) — MAC preserved; with v1.04, MAC changes consistently.
- Cross-referenced with INT-41256 (duplicate-dock-mac-enum-loop) — similar symptoms but different root cause (driver binding vs firmware override).

Temporary workaround tried:
- Manual MAC override in OS using netsh/PowerShell on host restores expected MAC and allows cert binding to complete. Not scalable for depot-returned fleet.
- Replacing dock with older firmware unit (v1.02) allows provisioning to proceed.

Next steps:
- Coordinate with depot to halt automated TB18D firmware push for now.
- Engage vendor support (Dell) with packet captures, vendor diag output, and example device IDs.
- Add an automated verification step in depot checklist to validate persistent MAC post-repair.
- Create an Intune detection rule to flag locally administered MAC addresses during enrollment as a pre-emptive block.
comments: Aisha Malik (2026-03-10): Reported after 7 devices failed post-repair provisioning this morning. Captured Intune correlation IDs and inventory mismatches. Raised to SRE for network evidence.

Ethan Chen (2026-03-10): Running controlled repro with 2 devices. Confirmed MAC flip when dock firmware v1.04 is applied. Temporarily pulled firmware bundle from depot staging. Placed hold with techops.

SRE - Priya Rao (2026-03-11): Collected switch CAM table, confirmed that MAC presented is locally administered (LSB of first octet = 1). We should treat this as firmware-induced override. Logged case with Dell ESCALATION ID: DELL-ESC-44321.

Depot - Marcus Li (2026-03-11): We pushed firmware as part of the 'dock refresh' workflow. Will stop the firmware step and quarantine affected docks for vendor return. Added a checkbox to the depot runbook to validate NIC MAC persistence.
Security - Lina Gomez (2026-03-12): Flagged as compliance risk. Recommend we block devices with locally administered MACs from auto-enrolling until resolved.
resolution_notes:
Workaround implemented: Depot halted automatic TB18D firmware pushes and replaced returned docks with known-good units (v1.02) for affected devices. Added temporary Intune enrollment detection to block locally administered MACs and route to manual remediation.

Permanent actions planned:
- Dell provided firmware reproducer and confirmed regression; vendor to issue hotfix or rollback guidance (ESCALATION DELL-ESC-44321).
- Update depot SOP to include 'verify host NIC MAC persistence' as a required step post-repair.
- Implement automation in the depot QA script to run netsh and compare MAC against asset DB before returning device.
- Create KB for helpdesk: steps for manual MAC override and when to escalate to hardware vendor.

Current status:
- Affected docks quarantined; 12 devices reprovisioned using replaced docks; user-facing impact reduced. Awaiting vendor firmware fix.
notes_for_follow_up:
- Verify vendor hotfix availability and test in depot staging before mass rollout.
- Add telemetry to provisioning pipeline to surface MAC topology mismatches earlier.
- Consider binding certificates to device serial + MAC hash to be more resilient to dock-forwarded NIC changes.
